scenario: AITA for shutting down conversation about babies? | Recently, my good friend (let’s call her B) was in town visiting and we went out for drinks at a fancy new bar with another friend of hers (let’s call her M), who I’d only met once before. We were on our first drink and having a great time, catching up on all sorts of things about our lives. Then, M started talking about someone she knows and the fertility struggles that she’s having, saying things about her “geriatric eggs” and how risky it all is at her age. Then, M grew wistful about how it was probably too late for her to have babies. For context, I’m older than any of them and have badly wanted a child for years, and fear it’s too late for me, which makes me super sad. B knows this. I said something abrupt like “this subject isn’t a good one for me” and tried to shift the subject to B’s new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned and M was upset, so I then said something like, “Did I offend you? That wasn’t my intention.” At this point, M was tearful, and said she was trying to open up and didn’t like being told to “shut up” and was going home because I made her very uncomfortable, and stormed off. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure M found a Lyft, and then came back. Am I an ass? It was my only chance to catch up with my friend and I wanted to keep the mood light, but the evening was ruined.

Let me start by going through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details. So, my friend B and I went out for drinks at a new bar with another friend, M, whom I've only met once before. We were on our first drink, having a great time catching up. Then M started talking about someone she knows who's going through fertility struggles, mentioning geriatric eggs and how risky it is at her age. She got a bit wistful about how it's probably too late for her to have babies. Now, I'm older than both of them and have wanted a child for years, fearing it's too late for me. This makes me really sad. B knows this. So, I said something abrupt like, "This subject isn't a good one for me" and tried to shift the subject to B's new life in the town she moved to. I could see that B looked concerned and M was upset, so I asked if I offended her, saying that wasn't my intention. At this point, M was tearful and said she was trying to open up and didn't like being told to shut up, so she was going home because I made her uncomfortable. She stormed off. B went with her to settle the tab and make sure M found a Lyft, then came back. I'm wondering if I was a "nass" (which I think is slang for "nervous wreck" or "idiot") in this situation. I wanted to keep the mood light and catch up with my friend, but the evening was ruined. So, the question is: Was I right or wrong to shut down the conversation about babies? And why? First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. M was opening up about her fertility struggles, which is a sensitive topic. She was sharing her feelings about it being too late for her to have children. I, on the other hand, have my own struggles with wanting a child and fearing it's too late. This makes me sad, and I tried to shift the conversation because it was triggering for me. But by doing so, I made M feel like she was being shut down. She felt uncomfortable and left. So, was my reaction appropriate, or was it insensitive? I think it's important to consider both perspectives. On one hand, I have the right to not be triggered by conversations that are painful for me. On the other hand, M was trying to share something personal, and my reaction made her feel invalidated. Maybe I could have handled it differently. Instead of abruptly shifting the subject, I could have acknowledged her feelings and then explained that the topic is difficult for me. For example, I could have said, "I'm really sorry to hear that you're feeling this way. It's a tough situation. For me, this is a sensitive topic because I've been hoping to have a child, and it's been a struggle. Maybe we can talk about something else for now?" That way, I'm validating her feelings while also setting a boundary. Alternatively, I could have asked her more about her feelings, showing empathy, which might have made her feel supported instead of shut down. But I was in a situation where I was already feeling sad, so it might have been hard to be supportive without getting overwhelmed. I also need to think about the group dynamic. B was there, and she knows about my situation. Maybe she could have helped mediate the conversation, but I was the one who reacted first. Another angle is to consider the intention behind my actions. I wanted to keep the mood light and enjoy catching up with my friend. But by shutting down M's feelings, I ended up making the evening worse. So, my intention was good, but the execution was flawed. I also wonder if there's a cultural or personal context I'm missing. For example, maybe in some cultures, it's not appropriate to discuss such sensitive topics in public settings, or perhaps M was expecting a certain level of support that I wasn't able to provide. In terms of personal feelings, I can see why I would feel defensive or sad when the topic comes up. It's a deeply personal issue, and it's natural to want to avoid pain. However, in social situations, especially with friends, it's important to balance one's own feelings with the feelings of others. So, in conclusion, while I had a valid reason for wanting to avoid the topic, my approach was too abrupt and didn't take into account how it would affect M. A more empathetic and communicative approach would have been better, allowing both of us to express our feelings without making the other uncomfortable.
